summary: Multipart/streaming request causes pin negotiation to fail and fallback to legacy variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when sending multipart streaming payloads (text + base64 attachments) to the chat generation endpoint during a canary rollout, the platform intermittently fails to establish model-version pinning for the session and instead routes requests to the legacy variant.

Impact:
- Several tenants at Lumina Health observed mixed outputs (new-model and legacy-model responses) for the same session when resuming a stream after an attachment upload.
- Apparent increase in quality regressions and customer-facing mismatches during the canary slice (1.2% of their traffic).
- No increase in 5xx errors, but higher-than-expected fallback routing and user confusion.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, canary rollout 14:00-16:00 UTC window on 2026-03-12.
- Customer sending multipart/streaming requests via SDK v1.7.2 through edge-proxy cluster ep-us1-a.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Create a chat session pinned to new variant (redwood-2.1-xl) via the standard session start call.
2) Send a series of streamed messages with a mixed payload: initial text blocks, then a multipart boundary with a base64-encoded clinical image, followed by more text frames in the same stream.
3) Pause the stream client for 6-12s (simulating upload overhead) and resume.
4) Observe that subsequent responses are served by legacy variant for 1-5 requests before pin resumes.

Observed behavior:
- Pin negotiation appears to succeed on session creation (server returns pin token).
- After multipart boundary is introduced and client resumes, we see a routing change where the session is served by the legacy variant (older model id) for several requests.
- Edge logs show a dropped pin-lease-renew attempt when the multipart boundary coincides with a keepalive/health probe.

Expected behavior:
- Multipart/streaming payloads should not interfere with pin lease negotiation or renewal; session must remain pinned to the selected variant for the lifetime of the session or until explicit unpin.

Workarounds attempted by customer:
- Shortening upload pause to <2s reduced incidence but did not eliminate it.
- Forcing re-pin via a session-patch call temporarily restores correct routing.

Attachments:
- Customer provided request/response headers and a trimmed HAR of the streaming session (attached to ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start pinned session to redwood-2.1-xl. 2) Stream alternating text and a base64 attachment in the same HTTP/2 stream. 3) Pause client 6-12s during upload, then resume. 4) Observe routing flips to legacy variant for several requests.
logs:
Edge proxy excerpt (ep-us1-a) around 2026-03-12T14:23:48Z:
- INFO  route_decision: tenant=lumina-prod session=abcd1234 pin_token=ok model_target=redwood-2.1-xl
- WARN  pin_lease_renew: tenant=lumina-prod session=abcd1234 reason=stream-chunk-boundary dropped=true probe_conflict=true
- INFO  route_decision: tenant=lumina-prod session=abcd1234 model_target=rwd-open-7b fallback_reason=pin_miss
- DEBUG serving-runtime: kvcache-lookup miss for session abcd1234 during multipart boundary
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: multipart boundary frames are processed by a different edge request handler path which timestamps/metrics differently, causing pin-lease-renew to race with health probes.
Reproduced internally: deterministic repro when injecting artificial pause + boundary frames in HTTP/2 stream across edge-proxy. Pin renewal RPC to orchestrator returns 409 (lease-refresh-conflict) under race.
Observed additional signals:
- Keepalive/health probe from orchestrator happens every 5s for prewarm probes. If probe and client resumed chunk coincide, edge refuses lease update and marks pin as stale for 1 interval.
- Orchestrator expected idempotent renew, but multipart boundary handler sets content-type flags that alter header ordering; orchestrator signature check rejects renewal when a specific header ordering is present (bug in header canonicalization).
Next steps proposed:
- Patch edge proxy to normalize multipart header ordering before sending renewal RPC (short-term mitigation).
- Add idempotent acceptance of lease renewals even if header ordering differs (orchestrator fix).
- Schedule controlled canary rollback window to test fix on canary slice during low-traffic hours.
